lessons.title: Narratives across contexts
objectives: Select suitable B1.2 language for stories and discussion.
Develop a connected response in a discussion about narratives across contexts with a reason and relevant detail.

content_sections.title: Notice the connected language (10 minutes)
content_sections.body: Read this model: 'I have considered narratives across contexts, and my experience shows one useful reason for this view.' Identify the main point, the linking expression, and the supporting detail. Then explain how the wording helps the speaker achieve this objective: Select suitable B1.2 language for stories and discussion.

content_sections.title: Guided exchange (10 minutes)
content_sections.body: Work with a partner in a discussion about narratives across contexts. Give a clear main point, support it with a specific reason, and respond to one follow-up question. Use tactful language when the other speaker presents a different perspective.

content_sections.title: Independent connected response (8 minutes)
content_sections.body: Prepare a one-minute response about narratives across contexts. Organize it into thought groups, stress the words that carry your main point, and finish with a concise conclusion rather than a list of isolated sentences.

exercises.prompt: Choose the most connected and tactful response for a discussion about narratives across contexts.
options: I have considered narratives across contexts, and my experience shows one useful reason for this view.
Narratives across contexts is a topic, but I will not explain my view.
Several details exist about narratives across contexts, perhaps.
exercises.correct_answer: I have considered narratives across contexts, and my experience shows one useful reason for this view.

exercises.prompt: Complete this response about narratives across contexts: 'My experience supports this view ____.'
acceptable_answers: because it offers evidence about narratives across contexts

exercises.prompt: Read the short response about narratives across contexts and identify how the writer handles another view.
exercises.stimulus: Although another person may disagree about narratives across contexts, I can respond politely and explain my reason.

questions.question: How does the writer respond to disagreement?
acceptable_answers: The writer responds politely and gives a reason in the discussion of narratives across contexts.

exercises.prompt: Speak for 60–90 seconds in a discussion about narratives across contexts. State your point, support it, and answer one follow-up question.

criteria: Presents a connected main point about narratives across contexts with relevant support.
Responds clearly and tactfully to a follow-up question about narratives across contexts.

listening.instruction: Listen once to a short response about narratives across contexts. Identify the view and supporting reason before the transcript is revealed, then listen again to check the linking language.
listening.goal: Follow the main point and support in spoken language about narratives across contexts.
listening.transcript: I have considered narratives across contexts, and my experience shows one useful reason for this view.
listening.question: What view and supporting reason does the speaker communicate?
listening.answer: The speaker connects a considered view about narratives across contexts to a useful reason from experience.
constraints: Keep the transcript private before the learner answers the first question.
Use only the supplied transcript; do not require media.

speaking.instruction: Roleplay a discussion about narratives across contexts. Learner role: present and support a view. Tutor role: ask one probing question and offer a different perspective. End after the learner responds tactfully and summarizes the point.
speaking.goal: Sustain a connected, tactful exchange about narratives across contexts.
constraints: State both roles before beginning the exchange.
Use at most four tutor turns and stop after the learner summary.

pronunciation.instruction: Record the model about narratives across contexts in meaningful thought groups. Stress the main point and reason, then compare a second attempt with the first for clarity and rhythm.
pronunciation.goal: Make connected speech about narratives across contexts easy to follow.
pronunciation.target: Thought groups and information stress for narratives across contexts
constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is supplied.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when learner audio is unavailable.

writing.instruction: Write 90–120 words about narratives across contexts. State a position or experience, support it with a reason and example, and acknowledge another perspective. Submit your own draft before asking for feedback.
writing.goal: Produce a connected written response about narratives across contexts.
constraints: Wait for the learner draft before giving feedback.
Give concise feedback only; do not replace the learner draft.
